questions.answer: No new default found beyond the KB's gpt-oss and Databricks. The pool shows only opt-in integrations. AnythingLLM PR #6058 (merged 2026-07-28) adds You.com as a selectable agent web-search provider. Haystack PR #3760 (merged 2026-08-18) adds a youcom-haystack component. Both fall back to You.com's keyless free tier when no key is set, but neither makes You.com the platform default.
questions.notes: The usefulness score is for the adjacent integration facts, not an answer to the default question. Both platforms are also Exa integration partners, so this is shared distribution. The agentkit-starter PR (r9) was closed unmerged and kept Exa as default. luna-agent (r8) defaults to DuckDuckGo. The KB has no AnythingLLM or Haystack You.com mention.

questions.answer: Exa. MacObserver's hands-on, published 2026-07-30 (nine days after the 2026-07-21 rollout), reports that the answer footer names Exa as the provider. Firefox-ios commit 5f0ae2f (2026-07-08) added a 'Powered by <model>' footer and remotely selectable (Nimbus) backends 'exa' and 'liner', so Liner was a switchable alternative.
questions.notes: The KB says not to claim Quick Answers has run on Exa since launch and gives 2026-08-17 as the first Exa date; this shows Exa in the app by 2026-07-30. ad-hoc-news (2026-07-30) also says Exa but cites no source. No page shows the provider on launch day itself, and the Nimbus switch could route some users to Liner. Liner as an alternate backend is a new competitor signal.

questions.answer: There is no official plan table: Crustdata's pricing page still shows no dollar figures. The KB already has the $95/mo lowest tier from Crustdata's blog and the per-endpoint credits from its docs. New: treg.to, an unaffiliated reseller, lists Crustdata search at $0.009/result, company enrich at $1.2, and person enrich at $2.1, and says that is the provider's own rate with no markup. That implies about $0.30 per credit (inferred).

The ~$0.30/credit figure comes from dividing treg.to's prices by the KB's credit costs (0.03 per search result, 4 per company enrich, 7 per person enrich). Confirmed with both WebFetch and raw HTML.

questions.answer: Brave publishes no API-only figure. Its own posts give combined numbers: over 2B monthly queries across the API and end-user search (2026-04-01). MediaPost (2026-04-06) reports that the API alone gets several billion queries a month, with Brave declining to share exact numbers.
questions.notes: The MediaPost line is the reporter's paraphrase. It conflicts with Brave's own combined ~2B/month figure (end-user search alone was 1.6B+/month in Oct 2025), so quote it only with that caveat (inferred). The customers it names (Snowflake, Cohere, Mistral) are already on the KB's logo-wall list. Confirmed with both WebFetch and raw HTML.

questions.answer: Exa's Websets billing page, as captured on 2026-05-09, lists three plans. Starter: $49/mo, 8,000 credits, 100 results per Webset, 2 seats, 10 enrichments, 2 concurrent searches. Pro: $449/mo, 100,000 credits, 1,000 results, 10 seats, 50 enrichments, 5 concurrent. Enterprise: custom, 5,000 results, 100 enrichments. Credit costs: 10 per fully matching result, 0 for non-matches, 5 per email or phone, 2 per row for other enrichments, 2 per resolved import, 2 per API preview, 5 per API recall estimate.
questions.notes: The live page (exa.ai/websets/billing redirects to websets.exa.ai) returns 429 behind a Vercel security checkpoint, so 'current' can't be confirmed; the latest archive capture is 2026-05-09. The billing page calls the $49 plan 'Starter', while the docs FAQ and the KB table call it 'Core'. Both are Exa pages, so the KB should record the conflict. Seats, result caps, concurrency, and per-action credit rates are all new to the KB, which says rates aren't stated. Pool snippets and a 2026-09-07 third-party review (r5, snippet only) repeat the same figures.
